title: Hard Wired: A Crash Course in Small College Football
author: David T. Nelson
target_audience: Sports enthusiasts, particularly fans of college football
Coaches and educators interested in athletics at the small college level
Students and graduates of small colleges
Readers interested in leadership and team culture
General nonfiction readers curious about American football subcultures
core_themes: Challenges and rewards of small college football
Resilience and personal growth through athletics
Resourcefulness in the face of limited funding and recognition
The role of football in shaping individual and collective identity
primary_purpose: To provide an inside look at the realities, struggles, and triumphs of student-athletes and coaches at small colleges, offering personal stories, insights, and lessons from life on and off the field.

structure_format.organization: Organized into chapters that each explore specific aspects of small college football, including memorable games, personalities, and key lessons
features: Analysis of coaching and team dynamics
Reflections on college athletics and life skills

key_concepts_lessons: Success in sports is not solely determined by resources or fame; grit and camaraderie are foundational.
Coaching at a small college requires adaptability, empathy, and creativity.
Athletes in small programs develop unique bonds and face distinctive pressures not seen at major universities.
Life skills gained through small college football—such as discipline, leadership, and resilience—translate beyond sports.
Recognition and support for small college programs can be meaningful for campus and community morale.
notable_features: Insider perspective from a coach/educator deeply involved in the sport
Focus on underrepresented and often-overlooked aspects of college athletics
Analysis of resilience amidst limited resources
cultural_historical_context: Published during a period of growing attention to the economics of college sports, especially following heightened awareness of funding disparities and athlete experiences during the COVID-19 pandemic. Sheds light on the often ignored world of small college football, contrasting it with the glitz of NCAA Division I programs.
reception_impact: Appreciated by readers for its authenticity and sincerity
Valued by coaches and educators for practical leadership lessons
Provides a perspective rarely captured in mainstream sports coverage
Encouraged dialogue about the value and future of small college athletics
comparable_titles: Season of Life by Jeffrey Marx
Friday Night Lights by H.G. Bissinger
The Last Shot: City Streets, Basketball Dreams by Darcy Frey
Meat Market: Inside the Smash-Mouth World of College Football Recruiting by Bruce Feldman
